text:
ellie: Heads-up, we're getting client reports of 5xx from hosted-api after the morning rollout. Spike started ~10:12 PST and correlates with the canary.
raju: seeing increased 502/504 from gateway too. Telemetry shows a jump in upstream timeouts to the model pool.
deploy-bot: Release r2026-03-17-451 canary started at 2026-03-17T10:08:12Z
support-lee: multiple customers opened tickets: high latency + errors during inference. Billing page shows a few failed charge attempts but mostly API errors.
sre-oncall: @raju can you paste a quick curl repro and a few request IDs so we can trace in proxy logs?
raju: cURL snippet and sample response below:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat token)" \
  -H "X-Client-ID: acme-123" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":50}'

HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 10:12:34 GMT
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":{"message":"upstream read timeout","id":"req_0a1b2c3d"}}
```
ellie: thanks. I see `req_0a1b2c3d` in gateway logs — it shows `504 read timeout` when talking to model-hosts, but owner header is truncated in the upstream call: `X-Orig-Auth: Bearer ...` becomes `X-Orig-Auth: Bear`.
kevin: that header truncation rings a bell — there was a small proxy header rewrite introduced in the canary to trim long headers for perf. Might be chopping off tokens for certain auth formats.
sre-oncall: if auth to model hosts fails we can get upstream 502/504. Can we repro locally by sending a long auth header?
raju: yes, quick test shows truncated header when header length > 128. Repro steps:
```
# simulate long token
TOKEN=$(python -c 'print("a"*200)')
curl -s -D - -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://canary-gw.internal/ping
# response contains 400 from model-host: "invalid auth"
```
support-lee: customers are seeing partial charges because some requests succeeded and others errored — triaging with billing engineering too.
ellie: immediate mitigation: disable the header-trim feature in canary and roll back canary-only change. @deploy-bot, can you pause the canary? :pray:
deploy-bot: Pausing canary for r2026-03-17-451... paused. Will stop new canary traffic within 30s. :white_check_mark:
kevin: pushed a hotfix to revert header-trim: `git sha: f3b2a1d` — suggest rollback for canary and schedule full rollback if errors persist.
sre-oncall: rolling back canary now to previous routing config. Running:
```
infractl rollout cancel --canary r2026-03-17-451 && infractl apply --config routing/prod-previous.yaml
```
raju: confirmed downstream model hosts now receiving full auth header. Observability shows 5xxs dropping back toward baseline within 90s.
support-lee: updating tickets: told customers we're rolling back and investigating root cause. Added temporary mitigation to use shorter tokens as a workaround for affected customers.
ellie: action items:
- kevin: open PR to add header-length test + unit to proxy (owner: kevin)
- ra ju: validate no other header rewrites in pipeline (owner: raju)
- support-lee: coordinate billing follow-up and customer comms (owner: support-lee)
- sre-oncall: monitor for any residual 5xxs and confirm rollback stability (owner: sre-oncall)
kevin: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/proxy/pulls/789 (adds header-length guard + e2e)
sre-oncall: sending post-rollback telemetry snapshot to infra-channel. 5xx rate back to baseline ~5m after rollback. Will keep watching for 1h.
ellie: thanks everyone. We'll do a postmortem tomorrow with timeline and learneds. :memo:
support-lee: customers notified, marking urgent tickets as "investigating - rollback in progress".
raju: misc note — add a test for long auth tokens in the canary pipeline so deploys fail fast next time.
kevin: adding the test and a feature-flag gated rollout for header rewrite in next patch.
ellie: closing thread for now, will reopen if spikes reappear. :slightly_smiling_face:
